content.title: SpaceX Florida rocket launch to follow Artemis II. What time is liftoff?
content.text: Updated April 1, 2026, 5:11 p.m. ETNASA's Artemis II mission is scheduled to launch from Kennedy Space Center in Florida on Wednesday, April 1.The 10-day mission will send four astronauts on a journey around the moon and back.This flight is a crucial test for future crewed lunar landings.The SLS rocket launch may be visible across most of Florida and into parts of Georgia.Artemis II is a "go."All eyes are on NASA's massive Space Launch System rocket, which, after liftoff in Florida, may be spotted far beyond the launch pad.The space agency's SLS spacecraft is set to launch no earlier than 6:24 p.m. ET today, Wednesday, April 1, 2026, from Kennedy Space Center. This rocket launch near Cape Canaveral, Florida, will send four astronauts further in space than any humans before them.By the way, Artemis II isn't the only rocket launch from Florida this week. SpaceX is planning a much more routine rocket launch for Thursday, April 2 (see below).The second under NASA's multibillion-dollar moon program, the Artemis II mission will send three Americans and one Canadian on a 10-day journey around the moon and back. While no landing is in store for the astronauts, the mission serves as a vital test flight to lay the groundwork for humans to make it back to the surface in as little as two years.Along the way, the Artemis II astronauts will make history, venturing about 250,000 miles in space – further than the record-setting Apollo 13 mission – and seeing a side of the moon that no human has ever seen.As of 4:30 p.m. ET Wednesday, April 1, all signs are looking positive that the mission will get off the ground."NASA’s Artemis II closeout crew is now completing one of the most critical steps before launch: preparing and closing the crew module hatch to the Orion spacecraft," NASA said in a 3:17 p.m. update.Though rockets in Florida blast off from NASA's Kennedy Space Center or nearby Cape Canaveral Space Force Station, it's possible for spacecraft to be seen far beyond the launch pad, including in other states: In December 2023, the SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket was spotted from Boca Raton to Cedar Key to Myrtle Beach.And in February 2025, people in Fayetteville, North Carolina, posted photos and video of a Falcon 9 rocket after liftoff from Cape Canaveral, Florida. More recently, in February 2026, a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket was seen about 150 miles away from Cape Canaveral in West Palm Beach, Florida.Pending weather conditions and cloud cover, the Artemis II mission's SLS rocket launch could be visible for most of Florida to parts of Georgia, according to NASA.In Florida, we can best see this moment in person, particularly if you're anywhere on the Space Coast (Melbourne, Florida, area), the Fun Coast (Daytona Beach area) or the Treasure Coast (Vero Beach, Jensen Beach and Fort Pierce).Here's when and how to watch the Artemis II and SpaceX Starlink launches and the visibility map for tonight's historic Artemis II liftoff.What time is the Artemis II rocket launch from Kennedy Space Center in Florida?NASA's Artemis II mission: 3 NASA astronauts and a Canadian astronaut will venture around the moon and back during a 10-day flight, helping pave the way for future crewed lunar exploration missions. Towering at 322 feet tall, the SLS rocket will generate 8.8 million pounds of thrust, making it the most powerful spacecraft NASA has ever launched.Launch: 6:24 p.m. ET Wednesday, April 1, 2026, with a two-hour window.Launch trajectory: East.Launch location: Launch Pad 39B at NASA's Kennedy Space Center near Cape Canaveral, Florida.Sonic booms for the Space Coast of Florida: No.Live FLORIDA TODAY Space Team coverage: Starts hours before liftoff at floridatoday.com/space.The visibility map provided by NASA shows when and where your best chances are to see the rocket as it streaks into space.The SLS rocket is composed of a 212-foot core stage propelled by four engines powered by a mix of liquid hydrogen and liquid oxygen, as well as two 177-feet-tall solid rocket boosters mounted to the sides providing the bulk of the thrust – a measure of the amount of force used to push the vehicle off the ground – and giving a great show to those watching.Which cities can see NASA Artemis II rocket launch from Kennedy Space Center in Florida?NASA provided a helpful graphic (see above) that shows the Atlas V rocket launch and its intended flight path and launch visibility. Note: Cities in the Space Coast of Florida, which is in Brevard County and measures 72 miles of coast, include Titusville, Mims, Port St. John, Merritt Island, Cocoa, Cocoa Beach, Melbourne, West Visibility may include Savannah, Georgia.The above guidelines are estimates based on the graphic provided by NASA.Photos of NASA Artemis II SLS rocket at Kennedy Space Center in Florida Watch Artemis II rocket launch from Florida with NASA on Prime VideoNASA content, including some rocket launches and the highly anticipated Artemis II mission from Kennedy Space Center in Florida, is available to watch through NASA+ on desktop, both from its official site and YouTube. The platform is also available to download as a mobile app on smartphones.All NASA+ content is also available to those who have Prime Video downloaded on any of their devices – whether it be a smartphone or smart TV.Watch NASA+ content with Amazon Prime VideoThe content, which does not require a Prime subscription to view, is one of Prime Video's FAST channels (free ad-supported television). Viewers can find it under Prime's Live TV section at the top of the screen when they open the app.Another Florida launch after Artemis II: SpaceX Starlink 10-58 on Thursday, April 2Mission: A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket will launch 29 Starlink satellites into low-Earth orbit.Launch window: 7:52 a.m. to 11:52 a.m. ET on Thursday, April 2.Trajectory: Northeast.Location: Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station.Sonic booms: No.Live FLORIDA TODAY Space Team coverage: Starts 90 minutes before liftoff at floridatoday.com/space.Contributing: Kim Luciani, USA TODAY NetworkFor the latest news and launch schedule from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station and NASA's Kennedy Space Center, visit floridatoday.com/space.
